verdict: Synchrony's total net revenue was flat at $3.8B — a bigger share of program profits went back to retail partners and credit costs rose 10% — so net earnings fell 17% to $892M even though purchase volume hit a record third-quarter level of $49.7B.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: total net revenue of $3,818M vs $3,823M a year ago

kpis.label: Net interest income
kpis.note: +2% vs a year ago; net interest margin 15.50%

kpis.label: Purchase volume
kpis.note: +8% vs a year ago, a record third quarter

segments.name: Net interest income
segments.note: Interest and fees on loans ($5,591M) and on cash and securities ($197M), minus $979M of interest paid on deposits and borrowings — up 2% on higher average loan receivables and lower funding costs.

segments.name: Retailer share arrangements
segments.note: The share of program profits paid back to retail partners — a contra-revenue line that grew 7% to $1,096M as program performance improved, taking a bigger bite out of net interest income.

segments.name: Other income
segments.note: Interchange revenue ($302M) and protection product revenue ($168M), minus $439M of loyalty program costs, plus other items — down 17% as loyalty costs rose.

opex.name: Employee costs
opex.note: Pay and benefits for the workforce — up 1% vs a year ago.

opex.name: Professional fees
opex.note: Outside professional and servicing fees — down 3% vs a year ago.

opex.name: Marketing
opex.note: Marketing and business development — up 14% vs a year ago.

opex.name: Information processing
opex.note: Technology and data processing — up 15% on technology investment.

opex.name: Other expense
opex.note: Everything else — up 47% vs a year ago, driven by higher operational losses.

otherDetail: Synchrony reports no separate 'other income' line below operating income — earnings before tax of $1,181M is revenue minus the credit-loss provision and operating expenses. The $28M equityM line is preferred stock dividends: net earnings were $892M, of which $864M was available to common stockholders, which is the basis for the $2.68 diluted EPS.
footerNote: For this lender, the provision for credit losses plays the role of cost of revenue, and retailer share arrangements (the profit share paid to retail partners) are treated as contra-revenue, so total net revenue is $4,809M + $105M − $1,096M = $3,818M. Net income here is the $864M available to common stockholders.

takeaways.title: Spending hit a record
takeaways.text: Purchase volume rose 8% to $49.7B — a record third quarter — and loan receivables grew 3% to $103.3B, with growth across all five sales platforms and the strongest gains from Gen Z and Millennial customers.

takeaways.title: Partners took a bigger share
takeaways.text: Retailer share arrangements rose 7% to $1,096M and the provision for credit losses rose 10% to $1,266M (a $30M reserve build, versus a $152M release a year ago). Together they more than ate the growth in interest income, cutting net earnings 17%.

takeaways.title: Credit held up, capital flowed back
takeaways.text: Net charge-offs improved to 4.79% of average loans from 5.16%, and loans 30+ days past due eased to 4.34%. The company returned $1.2B to shareholders in the quarter, including $1.1B of buybacks.
